paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as [0025], four digits on the page because the paragraph number is 25; the width was read off the page and not padded. Sentence spacing was measured in pixels rather than eyeballed: the gap after 'by context.' is 23px and after 'otherwise claimed.' is 21px against a word gap of 10 to 12px on the same lines, so both are transcribed as two spaces, matching the convention used on p02. The gap after 'e.g.' is 21px against a word gap of 18 to 20px on that same line, which is ordinary justification, so it is one space. The quotes around 'such as' are printed as curly typographic quotes and are kept as such. 'non-claimed' is a plain hyphen. Left margin line number 5 sits beside the 'all examples' line and is furniture, excluded.

paragraphs.zh: The following discussion provides many example embodiments of the inventive subject matter.  Although each embodiment represents a single combination of inventive elements, the inventive subject matter is considered to include all possible combinations of the disclosed elements.  Thus, if one embodiment comprises elements A, B, and C, and a second embodiment comprises elements B and D, then the inventive subject matter is also considered to include other remaining combinations of A, B, C, or D, even if not explicitly disclosed.

paragraphs.zh: The compound of formula (I), refers to mesotrione,2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)-2-nitrobenzoyl) cyclohexane-1, 3-dione, having the chemical formula:
paragraphs.en: The compound of formula (I), refers to mesotrione,2-(4-(methylsulfonyl)-2-nitrobenzoyl) cyclohexane-1, 3-dione, having the chemical formula:
paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as [0030]. Three printing details verified at 5x magnification. First, 'mesotrione,2-' is printed with NO space after the comma: the line carries nine ink tokens and eight inter-word gaps, which is one fewer than a space there would give, so the run-on is real and not a scan artefact. Second, 'cyclohexane-1, 3-dione' IS printed with a space after the comma, the same oddity p02 recorded in an earlier occurrence. Third, the moiety is spelled 'methylsulfonyl' with an f here, not the ph form the patent uses elsewhere; kept as printed per brief section 8. The line break falls after the existing hyphen in '(methylsulfonyl)-2-' and the next printed line opens 'nitrobenzoyl)'. The two halves are joined with NO space, departing from brief rule 3's join-with-a-single-space, because that hyphen is a locant hyphen inside the chemical name and inserting a space would split the substituent name into something the page does not say. This paragraph ends with a colon announcing a chemical formula, and that formula is NOT on this page: the last inked pixel row on the page is row 2003 of 2338 and every row below it is blank, checked programmatically, so the structure it points at must be drawn on p10.png.
